title: Add offline bundle signing step to CI/CD with protected keys + publishing conventions
creator: Sahana Iyer
project: Redwood Private: On-prem offline artifact signing
description:
Context
Air-gapped / offline installs for Redwood Private require deterministic offline bundles that can be verified without network access. This ticket covers the CI/CD changes to produce a signed bundle (manifest + signature envelope) with strong key custody controls, auditable approvals, and clear artifact publishing conventions.

Goal
Introduce a signing step in the Private release pipeline that:
- Signs the canonical bundle manifest (and only the canonical bytes) with a Redwood-controlled offline-bundle signing key.
- Keeps private keys out of build workers; signing happens via a protected KMS/HSM-backed key.
- Produces an auditable trail: who approved, what commit/build, what manifest digest, what key id.
- Publishes artifacts (bundle tarball, manifest, signature) using consistent paths/naming so the installer preflight can verify them reliably.

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Customer-managed signing roots / customer-signed bundles (deferred).
- Redesigning the bundle layout itself (tracked in ENG-4821 + packaging tickets).

Proposed implementation (pipeline)
1) Build step (deterministic)
- Generate offline bundle (tar.gz or zst) and bundle manifest from a clean workspace.
- Enforce deterministic settings (timezone/locale, sorted file lists, stable tar options, normalized permissions).
- Compute SHA-256 digest of the canonical manifest bytes and store as build output.

2) Attestation inputs (min required)
- build_id (monotonic), git SHA, tag (if release), build timestamp (UTC), builder identity, manifest_sha256, bundle_version.
- signing_key_id / key fingerprint and rotation epoch.

3) Signing step (protected keys)
- Use GitHub Actions OIDC -> Redwood Cloud KMS (or equivalent internal KMS) to request a single signing operation.
- No private key material is ever exported to CI.
- Signing job runs in a locked environment with:
  - dedicated runner pool
  - reduced egress (only artifact store + KMS endpoint)
  - least-privilege service account "release-signing-operator"
  - mandatory approval gate for production signing (see Approvals)

4) Outputs / publishing conventions
- Publish to the Private release artifact bucket/registry:
  - redwood-private-offline-bundle-${bundle_version}-${build_id}.tar.zst
  - manifest.json (or manifest.cjson if canonical JSON format is used)
  - manifest.sig (detached signature)
  - manifest.cert (optional, if we use cert-based signing) OR signing-metadata.txt
  - checksums.txt (sha256 for the bundle tarball + signature files)
- Additionally, publish a minimal "bundle-index" record keyed by build_id for support/release tooling.

5) Release gating
- The release train must fail closed if:
  - signature generation fails
  - signature verification (using the public key in CI) fails
  - manifest does not match the bundle contents (hash mismatch)
  - artifacts are not uploaded to expected locations

Approvals / separation of duties
- Staging: automatic signing with staging key (no manual approval), still requires verify step.
- Production: manual approval required before signing job can access prod signing key.
  - Required approvers: Release Eng (Connor O'Brien) + Security Eng delegate (Marcus Lin or Kevin Osei) OR Security leadership if policy requires.
  - CI stores the approval artifact (GitHub environment approval record + build log pointer) and links it in release notes checklist.

Key custody expectations
- Key stored in KMS/HSM-backed system.
- Access via OIDC + short-lived token; no long-lived secrets in CI.
- Key usage is logged (KMS audit logs) and correlated with build_id.
- Rotation support: allow selecting key by key_id/epoch; pipeline can sign with latest active key and include key id in signing metadata.

Open questions
- Final signature envelope format depends on ADR-0147 (detached signature vs embedded / DSSE). Pipeline changes here should match the chosen scheme.
- Whether to include an additional SLSA provenance attestation for the bundle build itself (nice-to-have for v1; not required for GA if it risks timeline).

Acceptance criteria
- A production release run generates manifest + signature with no private key material present on runners.
- Build logs clearly show manifest digest, key id, and artifact locations.
- CI verifies the signature as part of the workflow (using the public key bundle/trust store) before publish.
- Release gating (ENG-4862) can assert "signed bundle present" and block release if missing.
- Runbook notes for failures are added (link to CI doc + common failure modes).

Test plan
- Unit-ish: script tests for canonical manifest generation (stable bytes) and signature verify.
- Integration: run pipeline in staging with tamper cases (modified manifest, missing file, swapped signature) and confirm fail-closed.
- Regression: rerun same input build twice and compare manifest bytes + digests (expected identical if build inputs unchanged).

Rollout
- Land behind a feature flag in pipeline: SIGN_OFFLINE_BUNDLES=true.
- Enable in staging release train first for 1 week.
- Enable in production for RC builds, then GA.

comments: 2025-11-01 (Connor O'Brien): Agree P0. We should keep signing job isolated from the build job. Build job produces manifest + bundle, then signing job only downloads manifest bytes and signs. Avoid passing the entire bundle to signing job to reduce blast radius and runtime.

2025-11-03 (Marcus Lin): Security requirement: signing key access must be via OIDC + KMS, no base64 private key in secrets. Also require explicit environment approval in GitHub for production key usage. Please document which roles can approve and how evidence is retained.

2025-11-08 (Sahana Iyer): Draft workflow created in staging. Noticed tar output was non-deterministic due to file mtime; fixing with tar --mtime and sorted inputs. Will also pin compression level for zstd.
2025-11-18 (Kevin Osei): Please include key id + manifest digest in an easy-to-parse text file published alongside artifacts. Support and auditors will ask for this in offline environments.

2025-12-12 (Neha Kapoor): From ops side: add retry logic around KMS signing call (we’ve seen transient timeouts). But do not retry on "permission denied" or "key disabled". Also emit a metric/event for signing latency so we can track pipeline SLOs.

2026-01-10 (Jordan Lee): Canonicalization constraints: pipeline must sign the canonical manifest bytes produced by the manifest tool. No JSON re-serialization in the workflow step. Treat the manifest as an opaque byte stream after generation.
2026-01-15 (Connor O'Brien): Moving to In Review. Remaining item: confirm approval policy in the key ceremony doc and update the GitHub environment approvers list to match.
